raw.assessment: The incumbent provides staffed key access and telephone/in-person reservations; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Its eight-week target remains unproven: total needs and acceptable alternatives are unmeasured, three conflicts occurred, and observed administration averaged 127.5 minutes/week (H4-O3, H4-O4, H4-O6). The strongest account is that familiar repeating allocations provide some predictability, while incomplete demand records and inconsistent booking records limit coordination. A concrete limit to a simple spare-capacity explanation is H4-O3: six declined requests concentrated on Tuesday/Thursday evenings. Aggregate 68% reservation and late/missed sessions do not establish usable capacity in those windows (H4-O2); unspecified equipment also prevents treating rooms as interchangeable (H4-O5).

openings.claim: Inherited 90-minute allocations may exclude feasible rehearsals by mismatching actual duration, time-window, and equipment requirements.
openings.delta: Distinguish reallocatable time from genuine peak-time or piano scarcity before changing bookings.
openings.prediction: If allocation mismatch matters, a demand-informed schedule will meet more stated needs within accepted windows using existing room-hours. If peak/equipment scarcity dominates, unmet needs will persist despite rearrangement.
openings.probe: Use short contact conversations to record weekly needs, minimum usable durations, acceptable windows, and equipment. Compare current bookings with a proposed schedule protecting both performances and each requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. Count only accepted alternatives; check feasibility before implementation.
assumptions: Contacts can represent group needs accurately.
Shorter rehearsals are useful only when explicitly accepted.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk calendar, with dated change entries and a read-back of room/date/time to the contact, may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Make the online copy traceable to confirmed desk changes while retaining telephone and in-person access.
openings.prediction: Calendar-disagreement conflicts should decline; the other two conflicts may persist if their causes differ. Added recording could increase administration.
openings.probe: For eight weeks, record conflict causes and weekly administration minutes alongside change entries. Compare divergence-related conflicts separately from other conflicting expectations; assess the total conflict and two-hour administration targets.
assumptions: Desk staff and volunteer can share the authoritative record during existing staffed hours.
No software purchase or participant account is required.

raw.assessment: Unused aggregate room-hours coexist with unmet requests, but usable alternatives and equipment needs are unknown. A combined allocation-and-confirmation mechanism is plausible; neither feasibility nor attainment of the eight-week targets follows from the observations.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: combine equipment-and-window-aware reservation exchange with a single committed booking revision checked at key collection. The named interface is the handoff from a proposed multi-group exchange to confirmed room-access rights. Obtain every affected group's consent by telephone or in person before committing the whole exchange; until then, existing reservations remain valid.
openings.delta: Acceptable-window matching could expose exchanges hidden by inherited bookings, while coordinated confirmation could make those exchanges dependable. Matching alone can increase conflicting expectations; a reliable ledger alone cannot discover better allocations. Together they may turn nominal spare capacity into usable rehearsal access without adding volunteer reconciliation work.
openings.prediction: If compatible exchanges exist, the combined mechanism will meet more stated needs than confirmation alone and produce fewer inconsistent room-access expectations than exchange planning alone. Exchanges must preserve every requesting group's weekly 60-minute entitlement, equipment suitability, staffed hours and both booked performances; actual rehearsal needs may exceed the entitlement.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record total needs, acceptable windows and equipment. Replay the same requests under four conditions: current booking practice, matching only, committed revisions only, and both. Count fully met needs and simulate a change arriving between calendar copying and key collection; count contradictory authorizations and volunteer minutes. Trial only consented, constraint-preserving exchanges, using the desk record as authority and revision-marked calendar copies. Over eight weeks test the stated 90% needs, fewer-than-two-conflicts and two-hours-per-week targets. If no feasible exchange emerges, reject the allocation-benefit hypothesis.
assumptions: Some groups have acceptable alternatives and consent to exchanges.
The staffed desk can maintain one authoritative record and communicate committed changes through existing channels.
Protecting weekly entitlement is feasible within the supplied capacity; the mechanism cannot resolve an infeasible demand pattern.

openings.claim: Inherited 90-minute allocations may mismatch usable durations, windows and equipment.
openings.discriminator: Accepted rearrangements improve needs coverage; persistent peak/piano scarcity limits benefit.
openings.probe: Ask contacts for total needs, minimum useful durations, windows and equipment; compare current and feasible proposed schedules, counting only accepted alternatives.
openings.uncertainty: Contacts may misrepresent needs; 68% reserved and missed sessions do not establish usable spare capacity.

openings.claim: An authoritative desk calendar, dated changes and room/date/time read-back may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.discriminator: Calendar-divergence conflicts decline; other causes may persist.
openings.fit: Preserves telephone/in-person access without accounts or purchases.
openings.probe: Trace online copies to confirmed changes; track conflict causes and weekly administration for eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Desk coordination is unproven; recording may increase workload.

openings.claim: Window/equipment-aware exchanges plus committed revisions checked at key collection may jointly improve access and reliability.
openings.discriminator: Combined operation outperforms confirmation alone on needs and matching alone on contradictory authorizations.
openings.fit: Obtain all affected groups' consent before committing an entire exchange; existing reservations remain valid until then.
openings.probe: Replay identical requests under current practice, matching, revisions, and both; simulate a change between copying and key collection. Count fully met needs, contradictory authorizations and minutes. Trial consented exchanges with revision-marked copies.
openings.uncertainty: Alternatives and consent may be absent; no feasible exchange rejects the allocation-benefit hypothesis.

post_distill.decision: Probe feasibility first. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, requested weekly 60-minute entitlements, existing equipment, no new fees, both performances and offline booking/change channels. Entitlements may fall short of actual needs. Eight-week acceptance: at least 90% stated needs within accepted windows, fewer than two conflicts, administration at most two hours/week. Synthetic observations establish neither feasibility nor target attainment.
